details: Bitcoin's price has fallen below $77,000, experiencing a significant technical breakdown. This decline is accompanied by substantial outflows from institutional Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), with approximately $1 billion leaving these products in the week ending May 17. This "risk-off" sentiment among institutional investors is driven by rising U.S. Treasury yields, escalating geopolitical tensions, and renewed inflation fears, pushing capital away from risk assets across global financial markets.
title: Bitcoin Drops Below $77K Amid ETF Outflows and Macro Headwinds

details: Government bond yields worldwide, including U.S. Treasuries, German Bunds, and Japanese government bonds, have surged to multi-year highs. This global bond sell-off reflects growing investor concerns about persistent inflation, particularly fueled by rising energy prices. Markets are increasingly pricing in a "higher-for-longer" interest rate environment, with some analysts now anticipating a more than 50% chance of a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike by December, a notable shift from earlier expectations of rate cuts.
title: Global Bond Rout Deepens as Inflation Concerns and Rate Hike Bets Mount

details: Escalating geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran, including recent threats from former President Trump, have pushed oil prices significantly higher, with Brent crude surpassing $110 a barrel. This rise in energy costs intensifies global inflation concerns, contributing to the broader risk aversion observed in financial markets. The elevated inflation outlook increases the pressure on central banks to maintain or even raise interest rates, further impacting market sentiment.
title: U.S.-Iran Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher, Fueling Inflation Fears
